subject: Request for limited SLA grace period and modified remedy — NimbleHealth pilot
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nimblehealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: NimbleHealth Legal <legal@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for pilot — request for temporary grace and reduced credits

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the NimbleHealth team is excited to move the pilot into production next week. We ran a short traffic spike simulation and identified one concern: our workflows are sensitive to brief multi-second tails on inference during heavy-concurrency windows.

Commercial ask: for the 90-day pilot we need a temporary adjustment to the uptime SLA and the service-credit schedule while we ramp traffic. Specifically: a pilot-level availability target of 99.7% (vs. standard 99.9%) for the first 60 days with a capped remedy that removes automatic percentage-of-spend credits and replaces them with a technical remediation plan + one-time service credit not to exceed $X.

We understand this is outside standard terms — we wanted to surface it early so Redwood can evaluate operational and financial risk. We can share the spike logs and internal impact notes.

Can you route this to deal desk / execs for consideration? We have a legal review starting Monday and an internal deadline to confirm the pilot terms by end of week.

Appreciate your help,
Samir
Samir Patel
CTO, NimbleHealth
Attachment: pilot-usage-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: SLA ask for pilot — request for temporary grace and reduced credits

Team — forwarding NimbleHealth's request. Quick context: they've got an urgent legal deadline; pilot is strategic (large health-data pipeline, good reference potential).

Their ask in short: 60-day temporary drop to 99.7% uptime for the initial pilot and swap the automatic spending-based credit for an engineering remediation plan plus a one-time capped credit. They are explicit that this is only for the 90-day pilot ramp and they will revert to standard SLAs for any committed capacity.

Questions for deal desk / finance / legal:
- Operational: can the platform safely support a temporary, pinned lower SLO for a single account (traffic isolation controls + monitoring)?
- Legal: any showstoppers on removing standard automatic credit triggers and replacing with a remediation deliverable?
- Finance: what is an equivalent capped credit (ballpark) so we can offer something reasonable without creating precedent?

Attachments referenced by customer: pilot-usage-metrics.xlsx. Also drafted a short one-pager with a proposed limited remedy (attached).

We need either approval to proceed with the pilot terms or a counter by EOD Monday to keep their legal timeline intact. Can someone take point and advise?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the flag.

Initial thoughts:
- Ops/Engineering: temporary SLO pinning is feasible if we limit it to single-account routing to a dedicated pool for the pilot and enable tighter KV/cache settings to reduce the tail. That adds some operational overhead but is doable.
- Legal: removing automated credit triggers in favor of an engineering remediation plan + capped one-time credit is non-standard but we can document it as a negotiated pilot concession; legal to confirm language.
- Finance: need to quantify the cap. My preliminary guidance: cap at the greater of (1) 10% of expected pilot monthly spend or (2) a flat $15k one-time credit; that keeps exposure bounded while giving the customer comfort.

Requesting formal approval from Jonas (ops/legal authority) and Marcus (finance approval). If you approve, I'll draft a short addendum for NimbleHealth for their legal review and create operational runbook items to isolate the pilot. Need a green light by Monday COB if we want to hit their calendar.

Avery Johnson
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

Avery / Marissa — after reviewing the attachments and chat with Ops, I'm comfortable signing off on a constrained, documented pilot concession under these conditions: 

1) Duration: 60 days from pilot go-live; after 60 days NimbleHealth automatically reverts to standard 99.9% uptime terms for any ongoing usage or moves to a reserved capacity contract.
2) Remedy: replace automatic spend-based credits with a remediation plan (joint RCA + prioritized engineering fixes) plus a single capped credit not to exceed the greater of 10% of estimated first-month pilot spend or $15,000.
3) Isolation: Redwood Ops to route the pilot to a dedicated pool with guardrails (rate-limits and prefix caching) and provide a daily health digest for the first 14 days.
4) Documentation: Deal desk to produce a one-page addendum and SLO waiver memo signed by customer legal; no change to public SLA docs.
5) Precedent control: Mark this as a one-off pilot concession in SFDC and flag in Deal Desk handbook — any repeat asks will require VP-level approval.

Marcus — Marcus, please confirm the finance cap is acceptable. Lauren — CS, please prepare the onboarding checklist and daily health digest template.

If both Marcus and Marcus' finance team and NimbleHealth legal accept the addendum language, this is approved. Avery, please draft the addendum and loop in Legal for final terms. Marissa — relay to Samir and ask them to confirm acceptance of the conditions.

Jonas Weber
VP, Technical Operations | Redwood Inference
